items.title: States' subsidy, cash transfer outgo jumps from 16% to 21% of revenue receipts in 5 years: Report
items.summary: States' spending on subsidies and transfers has risen significantly over recent years and is expected to continue growing. By 2026-27, states are estimated to spend around 1 percent of GDP on cash transfer schemes. Major contributors to this increase are power subsidies and unconditional transfers for various beneficiaries, including women and farmers. States such as Andhra Pradesh and Chhattisgarh are among the highest spenders in these categories.

items.title: ONGC gas leak in Andhra Pradesh's Konaseema forces evacuation of around 800 people
items.summary: A gas leak occurred at an ONGC gas well in Geddada, prompting the evacuation of around 800 residents. Authorities cordoned off a 1 km radius around the well and diverted traffic along National Highway 216. Local officials instructed residents to avoid electrical appliances and gas stoves to prevent ignition. Continuous monitoring revealed zero gas concentration at the assessed locations after the leak began.

items.title: India, Philippines discuss defence, trade ties as PM Modi meets President Marcos Jr.
items.summary: Prime Minister Narendra Modi and President Ferdinand R. Marcos Jr. discussed enhancing cooperation in various sectors. They acknowledged the momentum in bilateral relations, particularly in defence and investment areas. The two leaders reflected on their previous meetings, emphasising the importance of their strategic partnership. India aims to expand its engagement with Southeast Asian nations through diverse initiatives.

items.summary: Fed Chair Kevin Warsh has flagged three possible outcomes of the AI revolution: faster economic growth through productivity gains, widespread job displacement due to automation, or an economic slowdown if investments and market expectations fail to deliver promised returns.

items.summary: FICCI has recommended that the long-term capital gains (LTCG) tax exemption on listed securities be restored. It is also batting for a calibrated increase in securities transaction tax (STT).

items.summary: India's GDP is expected to grow by 7.3% this financial year and 7.7% in the next quarter, S Mahendra Dev, Chairman of EAC-PM said. Sustained export momentum and improving foreign investment are crucial for this growth, he added.

items.title: India backs fair trade but won't allow unfairly priced imports to hurt steel sector: ISA
items.summary: Naveen Jindal, President of the Indian Steel Association, highlighted the importance of fair trade for the steel industry. He noted that India's steel sector can expand significantly by 2030-31 if challenges are addressed. Jindal emphasized embracing technology, particularly artificial intelligence, to improve operations and sustainability. Concerns were raised regarding Chinese steel exports and trade barriers posed by developed economies.

items.title: South Korea will suspend all aircraft operation for 35 minutes and markets will open late. Here’s why
items.summary: South Korea will suspend aircraft takeoffs and landings nationwide for 35 minutes on Thursday to minimize noise during a college entrance exam.

items.title: VB-GRAMG may cost states up to six times more than MGNREGA: Report
items.summary: The new rural employment scheme VB-GRAMG was estimated to cost states six times more than MGNREGA. Larger states like Bihar, Madhya Pradesh, Maharashtra, and Uttar Pradesh would face additional expenditures of Rs 2,000-3,000 crore. The Centre and states would share costs under VB-GRAMG, raising state financial burdens significantly. A state's share would depend on the 16th Finance Commission's devolution parameters.

items.title: Govt says Xiaomi, Flextronics hid royalty deals in tariff fight
items.summary: The Indian government has accused Xiaomi India and contract manufacturer Flex of failing to fully disclose royalty arrangements, as it seeks to recover unpaid customs duties and penalties. The dispute could cost Xiaomi more than $150 million and centres on whether royalty payments to technology partners should be included in the value of imported smartphone components. The Supreme Court is hearing Xiaomi's challenge.

items.title: BMW bets on luxury Alpina brand to woo wealthy Indian buyers in challenge to Mercedes
items.summary: The German carmaker will roll out Alpina as a "standalone brand" across 10 Indian cities and has started recruiting candidates for a network strategy role that includes selecting dealer partners, analysing competition and planning a rollout, according to a job posting on LinkedIn.

items.title: Indian technology companies widen their European footprint, from services to strategy
items.summary: Indian technology companies are broadening their European presence beyond traditional IT services, with Paris Region emerging as a strategic hub: 30% of France’s GDP, a dense research ecosystem anchored by Paris-Saclay and 89 Indian companies already established. Choose Paris Region, which has a permanent office in Mumbai, leading a delegation to the Bengaluru Tech Summit (17-19 November) to deepen this India-Europe strategic corridor.

items.title: Reliance plans to invest about $1.6 billion to build new biogas plants
items.summary: Reliance Industries is set to invest about Rs 15,000 crore in the establishment of nearly 100 compressed biogas plants in India by 2030. With 45 biogas plants already in operation, Reliance plans a substantial increase by March 2027 to further support the nation's energy mix goals.

items.title: UPI and the trust pact in its second act
items.summary: As tap-and-pay, UPI AutoPay mandates and agentic commerce take hold, more payments in India will go through without a customer entering a PIN or approving each transaction. At a closed-door roundtable hosted by Mindgate Solutions with PayU, industry leaders examined what that shift demands of payment providers and merchants, and who pays for it. Read on for the trends to watch.

items.title: India, other major APAC nations to maintain strong prudential oversight: Moody's
items.summary: Moody's Ratings suggests that key Asia-Pacific countries are set to uphold strong prudential supervision, which acts as a bulwark against excessive risk-taking and reinforces banks' capital buffers. This stability projects a positive outlook for global banks in 2027, supported by resilient macroeconomic conditions that exhibit their adaptability in adverse circumstances. The upcoming year will see six defining themes influencing bank credit quality.

items.title: UPI’s free era is ending. Who pays, who earns, and who gets left behind?
items.summary: A slice of UPI is likely to stop being free in the future. At a closed-door roundtable in Bengaluru, the people who build, lend and collect on India’s favourite payments rail debated what this means for merchants, TPAPs and the economics of the ecosystem. Read on for the sharp insights.

items.title: Budget 2027: FM Sitharaman chairs third pre-Budget consultation with manufacturing sector leaders
items.summary: Nirmala Sitharaman chaired the third pre-Budget consultation meeting for the Union Budget 2027-28 in New Delhi. The meeting included representatives from the manufacturing sector and senior government officials providing suggestions. This exercise aims to gather inputs from various economic sectors to shape the Budget's priorities. The Union Budget is scheduled for presentation on February 1, 2027, along with the Economic Survey.

items.title: Air India, Airbus to develop voluntary corporate SAF programme
items.summary: Air India and Airbus are collaborating to develop a voluntary Sustainable Aviation Fuel programme for the aviation sector. The feasibility study will explore methods to reduce emissions linked to air travel. The Indian government plans to mandate a 1 percent blending of SAF in jet fuel by 2027. Investments of USD 70-85 billion are anticipated to support SAF production by 2040.

items.title: Odisha govt hikes Dearness Allowance by 3% for state employees
items.summary: Odisha Chief Minister Mohan Charan Majhi announced a three percent hike in Dearness Allowance for government employees. The increase raises the DA from 60 percent to 63 percent, effective from July 1. Pensioners will also benefit from the same three percent increase in Dearness Relief. Approximately 8.5 lakh government employees and pensioners will receive this additional financial support. Payments reflecting the increased DA will be included in the November salary.

items.title: Anil Agarwal warns ONGC's takeover of Vedanta's oilfield risks denting investor confidence
items.summary: Vedanta chairman Anil Agarwal has warned that the transfer of its producing Cambay offshore oil and gas block to ONGC could send the wrong signal to investors. Urging regulatory stability, Agarwal said Vedanta was committing $5 billion to boost oil and gas production. He called on the government to avoid disrupting existing operators as India seeks to cut energy imports.

items.title: JSW Steel CEO flags Chinese exports, trade barriers as key challenges
items.summary: JSW Steel's CEO Jayant Acharya highlighted the impact of Chinese steel exports on Indian steelmakers. He stated that tariff and non-tariff barriers in developed markets complicate the situation. Despite these challenges, domestic steel demand in India remains strong. Acharya emphasized the need for India to open more iron ore mines for adequate raw material supply. This initiative would support the future growth of the steel industry.

items.title: DRI searches Cipla's Mumbai office, Bhiwandi depot over imported drugs
items.summary: The Directorate of Revenue Intelligence's Mumbai zonal unit has searched Cipla's office in Vikhroli and its depot in Bhiwandi over the classification or exemption of an imported pharmaceutical finished product. Cipla said it cooperated with authorities and that the proceedings would have no material impact on its financials or operations.

items.title: Budget 2027-28: Govt to invite Gen Z for pre-Budget consultations; Sitharaman meets economists

items.title: India's CAD may touch 1.2% of GDP in FY27 as oil, gold demand pose risks: UBI
items.summary: India's current account deficit is projected to reach 1.2% of GDP in FY27, driven by oil prices, according to a report by Union Bank of India. The report emphasizes that high crude oil prices and gold demand could impact the external balance. Merchandise trade deficit widened to a significant USD 39.88 billion in October. Additionally, imports surged while services trade surplus remained nearly flat during the same period.

The Reserve Bank of India has promoted overseas dollar raising, but this could lead to vulnerabilities. Strengthening dollar reserves through debt might not address underlying economic issues effectively.

items.title: Centre hikes windfall tax on diesel, ATF exports; petrol levy unchanged — Check details
items.summary: This follows the previous revision on October 31, when the government raised the diesel export levy from ₹8.5 to ₹11.5 per litre and the ATF duty from ₹10.5 to ₹11 per litre, while completely scrapping a ₹2.5 per litre levy on petrol exports.

items.title: Wholesale inflation faces a triple squeeze from fuel, food and metals in FY27: Report
items.summary: India's wholesale inflation is currently anticipated to reach around 11 percent in FY27, surpassing earlier projections. Persistent pressures from energy and input costs alongside risks to food prices are significant factors. The report highlights that global commodity prices will greatly influence this inflation trajectory. A potential 25-basis-point rate hike by the Reserve Bank of India is also expected in December.

items.title: Egypt, India aim to hit $12 bn bilateral trade target within five years, says Foreign Minister Badr Abdelatty
items.summary: Egypt and India are aiming to increase bilateral trade to $12 billion over the next five years and expand Indian investment in the North African country, Egyptian Foreign Minister Badr Abdelatty said. The target was discussed during Commerce Minister Piyush Goyal's visit to Egypt with an Indian business delegation.
